Frequently Asked Questions

Research Peptides in Canada — Frequently Asked Questions

Thirty answers on buying research peptides in Canada — how to pay, what the two numbers on a certificate mean, how to check a vial against its lot report, how delivery works, and what research-use only actually commits you to.

Buying & Payment

From Eppix Labs, shipped from stock held in Canada and priced in Canadian dollars. More usefully: buy from any supplier that names the laboratory it tests with and publishes the certificate for the exact lot you receive, rather than one generic report per compound. That is a check you can run on us and on anyone else before ordering.

Interac e-Transfer sent from your own online banking, or credit card (Visa, Mastercard, American Express) paid through a secure hosted invoice link emailed after checkout. Card details are entered on the payment processor’s page and never reach this site. The payment methods page shows the exact e-Transfer fields step by step.

Yes, 5% off, because an e-Transfer costs us no card processing fee. It applies automatically when you select e-Transfer at checkout and stacks on top of the mix-and-match volume discount.

EPPIX. No compound names, no product descriptions and no indication of contents appear on your card statement, and the same is true of the parcel itself.

Yes. Mix and match vials across the catalogue for a volume discount applied automatically in the cart from three vials, rising to 20% at ten — they do not have to be the same compound, and the current tiers are shown in the cart as you add. For larger volumes, contact us directly.

Products & Quality

The standard is 99% or higher, measured by HPLC on each specific lot with mass spectrometry confirming identity. The figure published on a certificate is the result for that lot alone — it is not an average across the catalogue and it is not carried over from a previous batch of the same compound.

Yes, by independent accredited analytical laboratories, primarily Janoshik Analytical. The testing laboratory is named on each certificate rather than left as a generic "third-party tested" claim, and each report can be opened on that laboratory’s own portal.

Purity tells you what fraction of the material in the vial is the compound on the label. It tells you nothing about how much is in there. Measured content is the actual quantity the laboratory found, against what the label claims — so a vial can be 99.8% pure and still be short-filled. Both figures are published for every tested lot; most suppliers publish only the first.

Lyophilized (freeze-dried) powder in sealed vials, which is the most stable form for storage and transit. Vial sizes vary by compound and are listed on each product page.

Lyophilized vials keep at -20°C for long-term storage and tolerate ambient temperature during shipping. Once reconstituted, store at 2-8°C and use within the window given in the product documentation. The storage guide in the research library covers this in more detail.

They do not differ in what arrives — a 5-pack is five of the same single vials, drawn from the same stock and the same lot where possible. The difference is only the price: the volume discount is applied for you rather than requiring you to add five vials to the cart yourself.

Certificates & Verification

A report from an independent laboratory confirming the identity, purity and measured content of one specific batch. The key word is batch: a certificate that is not tied to a lot number describes some material the seller once had, not the material in your hand.

Every vial carries a printed lot code. Enter that code on the verification page, or find it in the certificate library, and the independent report for that exact batch opens — measured purity, measured content against the labelled amount, the testing laboratory and the test date.

Yes, and you should. Each certificate links through to the testing laboratory’s own portal, where the same report is served by the laboratory rather than by us. A supplier that only ever shows you a PDF hosted on its own site is asking you to take its word for the contents of that PDF.

Look for four things: no lot number, or one that does not match your vial; no named laboratory; no test date, or one long predating the batch; and purity quoted without measured content. Any of those means the document is not evidence about the vial you are holding. There is a full walkthrough in the research library.

Yes. Previous lots stay published rather than being replaced when a compound is restocked, so you can compare results across batches over time on that compound’s certificate history — including for a vial you bought months ago.

Shipping & Delivery

Across Canada only, to every province and territory Canada Post serves. Stock is held domestically, so nothing you order crosses a border. Researchers in the United States are served by our US store.

Orders placed before 4 PM MT ship the same business day by Canada Post Xpresspost, typically arriving in one to two business days to major centres and a little longer to remote addresses. Every parcel is tracked.

Free on orders over $200 CAD, applied automatically. Below that a flat rate is shown in your cart before you check out. Free shipping and the mix-and-match volume discount can be combined.

Plainly. There is no branding, no compound name and no description of the contents on the outside of the parcel — only the shipping label.

Not for domestic transit. Lyophilized compounds are stable at ambient temperature over the one to two days a domestic shipment takes, which is why they are supplied freeze-dried in the first place. Refrigeration matters after reconstitution, not in the post. Guidance on handling deliveries in extreme winter conditions is in the research library.

Legality & Research Use

No. Everything sold here is strictly for in-vitro research and laboratory use. Nothing is intended for human or animal consumption, therapeutic application or self-administration, and nothing sold here is approved by Health Canada for any of those purposes.

Research materials of this kind are supplied for laboratory research use only and are not approved by Health Canada for human use. Buying them for legitimate in-vitro research is a different matter from buying an approved therapeutic, and the two should not be conflated. We sell under research-use terms and this is not legal advice.

We do not run a credential check at checkout, and we will not claim otherwise. By ordering you confirm the material will be used solely for lawful research purposes, and that attestation is the basis on which it is sold.

No, none, in any channel. We publish what the laboratory measured and what the peer-reviewed literature reports, and nothing about administration. Support cannot answer those questions either, and asking will not change the answer.

No. Stock is held in Canada and orders ship domestically, so there is no customs declaration, no CBSA inspection, no import duty and no brokerage fee arriving separately afterwards. Avoiding that is the practical reason Canadian researchers buy domestically rather than importing.

Orders & Support

Because of what these materials are, all sales are final and we do not accept returns. That is not the end of the conversation, though: if material does not match its published certificate, or an order arrives damaged or incomplete, contact support with the lot code and we will make it right.

Almost always this means the order number was not included in the transfer’s message or description field, so the deposit arrived with nothing to match it against and is waiting for someone to reconcile by hand. Email us the order number and the amount you sent and it will be matched. Nothing is lost.

While an order is still awaiting payment you can cancel it yourself from the payment page. Once payment has been received and the order is being packed, contact support quickly — anything not yet shipped can usually still be changed.

Through the contact page, 8 AM to 4 PM MT on business days. If your question is about a specific order or vial, including the order number or the lot code from the label gets you a useful answer in one reply rather than three.
